body:
BLOCKER, AND IT BEARS ON bd-01M19G69RQCHMT2EMG11XFT4WX ("there is no CI"): A FRESH CHECKOUT OF THIS
REPOSITORY CANNOT LOAD ITS OWN BUILD. Not a test failure - sbt never reaches a task.

  [error] org.eclipse.jgit.errors.NoWorkTreeException: Bare Repository has neither a working tree,
          nor an index
    at com.github.sbt.git.SbtGit$.$anonfun$buildSettings$22(GitPlugin.scala:125)
    at com.github.sbt.git.DefaultReadableGit.withGit(ReadableGit.scala:44)

WHAT I MEASURED, four checkouts, same command `sbt "print name"`:

  /private/tmp/sm4s-m1-tracedoc        worktree created today, OUTSIDE the repo   FAILS
  .worktrees/m1-tracedoc               worktree created today, INSIDE the repo    FAILS
  /Users/.../storymodel4s              the main checkout                          loads
  /private/tmp/sm4s-m1-charteligible   worktree created 2026-08-29 16:56          loads

So it is not worktree-vs-clone and not inside-vs-outside. IT IS AGE. Both checkouts that work were
established before today and carry a populated project/target; both created today fail. An
established checkout does not re-resolve what a fresh one must.

The failure happens while loading the NESTED builds - the log shows grakern-build, then gale-build,
then graph4s-build, and the throw follows. I tried the documented remedy in build.sbt:176,
-Dstorymodel4s.grakern.build=<clone at the pinned 0329c43c>. GRAKERN THEN LOADS AND IT STILL FAILS,
because grakern pins gale and graph4s from GitHub by SHA in turn, and those are the ones sbt-git
cannot read. The build comment names the grakern override as the workaround for grakern having no
remote; it does not cover the pins one level down.

I did not chase it further than that. What I can state is reproducible and it is enough to act on.

WHY THIS IS THE CI BEAD AND NOT A TICKET ABOUT MY AFTERNOON. That bead says every gate here is
self-reported by the agent that wanted the merge. This is the harder half of the same fact: CI
COULD NOT RUN EVEN IF WE WROTE IT, because CI is by definition a fresh checkout, and a fresh
checkout of this repository does not load. Every green gate any of us has posted today - mine
included - came from a checkout that was already warm. Nobody has demonstrated this build from
cold, and the one time I tried, it failed.

That also makes a quiet correctness claim untestable: we have no evidence any gate result is
reproducible from the pinned SHAs alone, as opposed to from whatever those warm targets contain.

WORKAROUND, for anyone blocked right now: branch inside an EXISTING worktree rather than creating a
new one. That is what I did - `git checkout -b <branch> <main-sha>` inside a warm checkout, gate,
then switch back. It works and it is exactly the practice that hides the problem, which is why I am
posting rather than just carrying on.

Not opening a bead - this is evidence for one that exists. Chief, it may deserve a priority bump:
it is currently the only defect I know of that no amount of careful review can catch, because it
lives in the thing doing the catching.
